outcome: As of 11 October 2026 the conjecture is still open: no counterexample and no proof turned up in any source. The window's events are a 2025 paper confirming it for four infinite families of values k (2^t, 2p^s, 2^2p, 2pq), an AI-credited (GPT-5.5 Pro) asymptotic for a neighbouring max/min preimage ratio (Erdős #694, May 2026), and two OpenAI manuscripts (Erdős #416 and #821, 6 October 2026) on neighbouring totient-count and multiplicity quantities; none of them settles whether a totient with exactly one preimage exists.
problem_asks: Whether every value of Euler's totient function has multiplicity greater than 1. Unpacked: is there any positive integer n with exactly one positive integer m satisfying φ(m)=n? That is the only part the statement asks; there are no bounds, sub-cases or further parts. Wikipedia's phrasing ('for every n there is at least one other integer m ≠ n such that φ(m)=φ(n)') compares n's own totient value and is the same question, since φ(n) is always in the image of φ. Values with no preimage at all (for example odd n > 1) are outside the statement. The answer is yes or no; a counterexample is a single n with exactly one preimage. Frozen wording: 'do all values of Euler's totient function have multiplicity greater than 1?'

events.what_happened: Carmichael first stated the claim as a theorem in 1907; the argument was faulty. In 1922 (Bull. Amer. Math. Soc., 'Note on Euler's φ-function') he retracted it and stated the claim as an open conjecture; he had also checked by hand that no m < 10^37 has multiplicity 1. Taken from the Wikipedia article and secondary sources; the 1907 and 1922 texts were not opened.
events.delivers: Claimed the full statement: every totient value has at least two preimages. The argument was faulty and was withdrawn by its author, so it establishes nothing.

checked_by.what_they_did: Found the error in his 1907 argument and retracted it in 1922, restating the result as a conjecture

events.directly_checkable: Carmichael's check below 10^37 is a hand computation; not reproduced here.
events.doubts: The 1907 argument was faulty, per Wikipedia and the author's own 1922 retraction. The 1922 note's text was not read.

events.direction: Claimed to prove the conjecture; withdrawn. Stated as open since 1922.

events.what_happened: Ford, 'The distribution of totients', Ramanujan J. 2 (1998) 67–151, announced in AMS ERA (1998). Re-posted to arXiv as 1104.3264 (v1 16 Apr 2011; v2 14 Jul 2013), described as 'New version of my 1998 article'. The 2011/2013 arXiv text contains: Theorem 5, the conjecture is equivalent to liminf V₁(x)/V(x) = 0, where V(x) counts totient values ≤ x and V₁(x) counts those with exactly one preimage; Theorem 6, if A(m)=1 then m ≥ 10^(10^10), with the bound obtained from computations in §7 extending Schlafly–Wagon; Theorem 7, liminf V₁(x)/V(x) ≤ 10^(−5·10^9), described as a variation of an argument of Pomerance; and the dichotomy that either there are no counterexamples or a positive proportion of totients are counterexamples. The 1998 text was not opened, so whether Theorem 6 is in the 1998 version is unknown.
events.revisions: arXiv 1104.3264: v1 16 Apr 2011 ('New version of my 1998 article'); v2 14 Jul 2013 (abstract lists a fixed small error in the proof of the lower bound for V_k(x), a fixed statement and proof of Theorem 3, and reorganisation; the abstract does not list the Carmichael theorems among the changes).
events.delivers: Reformulates the conjecture as liminf V₁(x)/V(x) = 0 (not proved). Shows liminf V₁(x)/V(x) ≤ 10^(−5·10^9): an upper bound, not zero, so not decisive. Any counterexample is at least 10^(10^10). Any counterexample, if one exists, is a positive proportion of totients. Does not decide whether a counterexample exists.
events.remains: Whether any totient value has exactly one preimage; whether liminf V₁(x)/V(x) = 0.

events.what_happened: Luca and Pollack, 'An arithmetic function arising from Carmichael's conjecture', J. Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 23 (2011) 697–714. Defines F(n) = #{m : φ(m) = φ(n)}; the conjecture is equivalent to F(n) ≥ 2 for all n. Proves that for every fixed ε > 0, K(n)^(1/2−ε) < F(n) < K(n)^(3/2+ε) for almost all n, with K(x) = (log x)(log log x)(log log log x). Journal receipt 14 May 2010, publication 27 Nov 2011. The date given is the receipt year because no earlier public posting was checked.
events.delivers: Typical-order bounds for the multiplicity function F(n), for almost all n. Does not decide whether F(n) ≥ 2 for every n.
events.remains: F(n) ≥ 2 for every n, which is the conjecture; in particular whether F(n) = 1 for some n.

summary: No source found by 11 October 2026 settles whether a totient value with exactly one preimage exists, and no counterexample or proof turned up. The historical record is finite-range checks (Klee 1947 below 10^400; Masai and Valette 1982 below 10^10000; Schlafly and Wagon 1994 below 10^(10^7)), a multiplicity-based lower bound (Ford 1998, any counterexample at least 10^(10^10)), and a density reformulation (Ford 1998, equivalent to liminf V₁(x)/V(x) = 0, with an upper bound of 10^(−5·10^9) that is not zero). Ford also shows any counterexample would be a positive proportion of totients. Erdős (1979, per citation key) showed any unique-preimage value would be one of infinitely many. Wikipedia (last edited 22 Dec 2025) states the conjecture is open and cites nothing after 2004. Inside the window, the events are: (i) Li and Sha (31 Jan 2024), a polynomial analogue over F_2[x], discounted by scope; (ii) Shannon, Shiue, He and Saito (thesis award 15 May 2025; NNTDM accepted 4 Aug 2025), which determines the preimage sets for k in four infinite families (2^t, 2p^s, 2^2p, 2pq) and reports the conjecture holds for those k. This is the only in-window event that confirms the integer conjecture for any values at all, and it is a restricted-family result; I found no independent review and no citing work. (iii) Erdős #694 (1 May 2026): Price posted that GPT-5.5 Pro claims a proof that max over n ≤ x of f_max(n)/f_min(n) ~ (e^γ + o(1)) log log x. Bloom and Sothanaphan checked the argument, and Lean formalisations exist (the proof file declares two axioms; I could not read the Overleaf write-up). This is a neighbouring quantity: the ratio is 1 exactly at unique-preimage values, but a maximum over n ≤ x says nothing about whether any such n exists. (iv) Erdős #416 and #821 (OpenAI repository, 6 Oct 2026): #416 counts totient values (V(cx)/V(x) → c), not preimages; #821 gives g(n) ≥ n^(1−ε) for infinitely many n, which is growth of multiplicities, not the existence of multiplicity 1. Both are attributed in the repository's README to 'an internal OpenAI model'; neither PDF was readable to me, and Bloom says #821 is not formalised and #416 is formalised. Close calls: whether a family-level confirmation (Shannon et al.) counts as a settled case under §2.1, which the judging pass must decide; whether #694 touches the problem, since its ratio is the Carmichael indicator at each n but the maximum over n does not test it. The AI record: #694 names GPT-5.5 Pro for the proof itself (authors' account: 'claims a solution'); Aristotle, Claude Code and Claude Opus 4.7 are recorded in the wiki and Lean files for formalisation only, so they are noted here and not in ai.systems. #416 and #821 name 'an internal OpenAI model' at repository level only. All other events report no AI system. Note: an unverified claim that a counterexample must exceed 10^(10^6) or that x < 10^1000000 has been checked (Encyclopedia of Mathematics, via a search snippet) was not confirmed at source and is not recorded as an event. The 1997 Saidak 'postcard proof' report (CRC, 1999) is recorded as an unsourced claim; the page I opened (t214) does not mention it, but c063 does. Nothing I found changes the status of the problem: open.
competing_reading: (1) Shannon et al. confirm the conjecture for infinitely many values of k, and under §2.1 'a single case settled counts'; a reader could treat the four families as a substantial partial resolution. Against this: the result is confined to four shapes of k, the full text and novelty were not checked, and no one has reviewed it. (2) Erdős #694 could be read as touching the problem because f_max(n)/f_min(n) = 1 exactly when n has a unique preimage, so the result is about the ratio that Carmichael's question tests. Against this: a bound on the maximum over n ≤ x of the ratio gives no information about whether the ratio equals 1 for some n, and the construction exhibits equal-totient pairs only at constructed n. (3) The 416 and 821 counts, V(x) and g(n), are the quantities Ford's density reformulation uses (V and V₁). An explicit asymptotic for V(x) could in principle feed a bound on V₁/V. No source makes that link, so I record it as not shown rather than as a bearing result.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The full text of Shannon et al. (NNTDM 31(3), 504–534, and the UNLV thesis PDF): the theorems, whether the four families were already known (for example from Ford's preimage results), and any citing paper. (b) The Overleaf write-up for #694 and the full Shashi456 Proof.lean: its contribution statement (does it say GPT-5.5 Pro produced the argument?), a full sorry count, and the list of axioms with #print axioms. (c) The PDFs of OpenAI's #416 and #821 manuscripts: their own AI disclosure and acknowledgements, their dates, and the status of their Lean files. (d) The erdosproblems.com status for #694 (SOLVED (LEAN) or none). (e) The 1998 Ramanujan Journal text of Ford's article, to see whether the 10^(10^10) bound and Theorem 5–7 are in the 1998 version or only in the 2011/2013 revision. (f) Any source for the 1997 Saidak report; if none exists, the claim is unsupported. (g) A 2026 search of arXiv math.NT for 'totient multiplicity' and 'preimage' listings after 26 January 2024 with citing-paper checks on Ford (1998) and Shannon et al. (2025).
